clue.text: Wild dog, drab, tailless and old

indicators.note: tailless says the word for drab loses its final letter

parts.note: drab means dingy, dull and dirty-looking

explanation.surface: A description of a feral dog: dull-coloured, missing its tail and getting on in years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailless' looks like part of the dog's description, but it cuts the Y from DINGY.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian dingo is a feral canine, a classic example of a wild dog.

clue.text: Pass round girl's testimonial

parts.note: Di, short for Diana, is a girl's name, with the possessive s
a tribute is an expression of praise, like a testimonial

explanation.surface: A girl's letter of praise is handed around.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass something round a group is to share it out or hand it out.

clue.text: She's made vows nobody heard

indicators.note: heard says the word is what is spoken aloud, not as written

parts.note: none means nobody, not one person

explanation.surface: A woman swears solemn promises that no one hears.
explanation.walkthrough: NONE is said the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman in a religious order takes vows of poverty, chastity and obedience.

clue.text: Neat wrapper husband's found in compound?

indicators.note: found in says the letter for husband sits inside another word

parts.note: an oxide is a chemical compound of oxygen
H is the abbreviation for husband; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A tidy wrapping is found inside a husband's chemical mix.
explanation.walkthrough: Neat is an old word for cattle, so a neat wrapper is a cow's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat means cattle, and the skin of an ox is what wraps that animal.

clue.text: Girl coming out with a set of data subject to discussion

parts.note: a deb, short for debutante, is a girl making her formal entry into society
a table is a set of data laid out in rows and columns

explanation.surface: A debutante emerges carrying a dataset, and it all becomes a matter for argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Something open to argument is arguable, a question people can dispute.

clue.text: Perform elegy outside school area

indicators.note: outside says one word wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: a dirge is a mournful song or elegy

explanation.surface: Someone sings a lament outside the school grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perform' reads as the definition of a song, but it means to carry out a duty; the elegy is the outer piece, not the thing performed.
explanation.definitionFit: To discharge a duty is to perform or carry it out.

clue.text: Degree thus regarded as essential

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a university degree
sic is Latin for thus, used to mark a quoted error

explanation.surface: A university degree is thus considered indispensable.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic and essential both describe what is fundamental and necessary.

clue.text: Lots more shakes — violinists play them

indicators.note: shakes says the letters of the preceding words are jumbled up

explanation.surface: More wobbling notes keep coming from the string players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shakes' rearranges LOTS MORE; it also hints at the trembling sound itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Tremolos are rapid repeated notes that string players produce with the bow.

clue.text: High flyer that's game to boycott beef?

parts.note: to black something is to boycott it, as in a trade union action
to beef and to grouse both mean to complain

explanation.surface: A rising star who is up for refusing to deal in beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High flyer' suggests an ambitious person, and 'game' willingness, but this is a bird shot as game.
explanation.definitionFit: The black grouse is a game bird, a high flyer in the literal sense.

clue.text: Milk supplier beginning to replenish jug

parts.note: a ewe is a female sheep, which supplies milk

indicators.note: beginning to says to take just the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A dairy supplier starts topping up the jug.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large jug with a wide mouth.

clue.text: Unusually shy sets in process of combining ideas

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters of the following words appear in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Someone shy is oddly drawn into a process of bringing ideas together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' rearranges the nine letters of 'shy sets in'.
explanation.definitionFit: In philosophy and general use, a synthesis is the combination of separate ideas into a whole.

clue.text: Obliterate part of opera selection

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A request to wipe out a portion of an operatic programme.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'operA SELection'.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase something is to wipe it out entirely, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: As some golfers play, all day and all night

definitions.meaning: a ... match in golf is one played going round the course in sequence of holes like the hours on a dial
continuously, for the full twenty-four hours

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means continuously through day and night, and also names a game played around a numbered sequence.

clue.text: Tainted openings accepted by almost all peacekeepers' female members

indicators.note: accepted by says one piece is taken inside another
almost all says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: UN, the United Nations, deploys peacekeepers
women are female members of a group
holes are openings

explanation.surface: Female UN peacekeepers have nearly all taken up dodgy openings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost all' drops the final letter of the peacekeepers' female members, and 'accepted by' places the openings inside what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwholesome means unhealthy or morally corrupting, much like something tainted.

clue.text: Carrot for one to make new blue film, having hesitation

indicators.note: new says the letters of the following words are made fresh in another order

parts.note: er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A carrot is pressed into service for a fresh blue movie, with some hesitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges BLUE FILM into UMBELLIF; 'for one' marks carrot as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: An umbellifer is a plant of the carrot family, bearing flat flower clusters.

clue.text: Baby, already wanting lunch, starts to cry

indicators.note: starts says to take the first letter of each of the preceding four words

explanation.surface: A hungry baby, wanting its lunch already, begins to wail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' takes the initial letters of Baby, already, wanting, lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: To bawl is to cry loudly, a direct synonym for the verb.

clue.text: Coded text Resistance buried amid fern, say

indicators.note: buried amid says one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: a cryptogam is a plant reproducing by spores, such as a fern; 'say' marks the fern as an example
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A secret message is hidden by resistance fighters among the ferns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buried amid' puts R inside CRYPTOGAM, the botanist's word for spore plants like ferns.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptogram is a piece of writing in code or cipher.

clue.text: Forwardness of new copper quietly leaving large town

indicators.note: new says the word copper is rearranged
leaving says a letter departs from the jumble

parts.note: P stands for piano, quietly in music
a city is a large town

explanation.surface: A new police officer shows cheek by quietly slipping out of the big town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes one P from the policeman's word, and 'new' reshuffles the other five letters (giving PRECO) ahead of the town.
explanation.definitionFit: Precocity is early development or forwardness, especially in a child.

clue.text: Extremely tacky setting for one embracing ruffianism

indicators.note: setting for says the outer letters frame the other piece like a setting holds a jewel
extremely says to take the first and last letters of the next word

parts.note: a hugger is one who embraces

explanation.surface: A gaudy setting for a cuddler reveals violent behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' takes T and Y, the first and last letters of 'tacky'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thuggery is brutal, violent behaviour, the conduct of a ruffian.

clue.text: Trap, possibly, with a couple of revolvers?

definitions.meaning: a trap is a light horse-drawn carriage, an example of a vehicle on two wheels
read whimsically, revolvers are wheels rather than guns, so this describes any vehicle with two wheels

explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle with two wheels, such as a bicycle or a pony trap, is described by this hyphenated term.

clue.text: Reportedly regretted lacking refinement

indicators.note: reportedly says the word is what is heard when spoken, not as written

parts.note: rued means regretted

explanation.surface: Someone is said to have regretted their lack of polish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reportedly' signals that RUED is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rude in the sense of crude or unpolished means lacking refinement.

clue.text: Tyrant initially serving in regimental HQ

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside another

parts.note: a depot is a regiment's headquarters

indicators.note: initially says to take the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A dictator begins his career serving at the regimental base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes S from 'serving'.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is an absolute ruler, a tyrant.

clue.text: Not all walk unsteadily after crew's dance

indicators.note: after says the words that come before in the clue follow the crew piece in the answer

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew, so the possessive gives eights
some means not all, a part of the whole
to reel is to stagger or walk unsteadily

explanation.surface: Some of a rowing crew stagger to the dance floor after their race.
explanation.walkthrough: An eight is a rowing crew, so the possessive gives the opening piece; 'after' places the other two behind it. The OCR text read 'steadily', but reeling is walking unsteadily.
explanation.definitionFit: An eightsome reel is a lively Scottish country dance for eight people.

clue.text: First of twenty, approximately, in trunk

indicators.note: first of says to take only the opening letter

parts.note: or so means approximately

explanation.surface: About twenty items are packed into a trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the trunk of the human body.

clue.text: Report of matinee actor once out of work?

indicators.note: report of says the word is what is heard when spoken

parts.note: a matinee idol was a handsome film star of old

explanation.surface: Word is that a former matinee star is now unemployed.
explanation.walkthrough: IDOL is said like the answer. The held text reads 'matin', but the wordplay needs 'matinee'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being without a job leaves you idle, unoccupied.

clue.text: Moving crowd compelled to work excessively

definitions.meaning: a herd or crowd of animals being driven along
the past tense of drive, as in to drive someone hard

explanation.definitionFit: A drove is a herd on the move, and to have driven workers is to have pushed them hard.

clue.text: Giving protection from cats and dogs in the fall?

definitions.text: Giving protection from cats and dogs in the fall?

parts.words: Giving protection from cats and dogs in the fall?
parts.note: raining cats and dogs is heavy rain, and the fall here is rainfall, not autumn or a tumble, so this is a coating that keeps downpours out

explanation.definitionFit: Something that keeps out heavy downpours is impervious to water from the sky.

clue.text: In error, like jury considering verdict

definitions.meaning: ... can mean mistaken, as in an estimate being ...
a jury is said to be ... while deliberating

explanation.definitionFit: Out means wrong in a calculation, and also describes a jury that has retired to deliberate.

clue.text: All the old retired, jolly bloke included

indicators.note: included says the following pieces are placed inside another
retired signals going backwards, so the archaic word is read in reverse

parts.note: ye is an old form of the
jolly is British slang for very, as in jolly good
bod is British slang for a person or bloke

explanation.surface: Everyone in the old folks' home has retired, a cheerful chap among them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns the old word around (EY), and 'included' places the other two words between its letters. Jolly meaning 'very' and bod meaning 'chap' are British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: All and everyone both refer to every person in a group.

clue.text: Time consumed by old party reversing coach

indicators.note: reversing says the whole assembled piece is read backwards
consumed by says one piece is eaten up inside another

parts.note: a rout was an old word for a large evening party or fashionable gathering

explanation.surface: An old political party, eaten up by time, backtracks on its coach.
explanation.walkthrough: T goes inside ROUT to give ROTUT, which 'reversing' turns around. 'old party' suggests a political party, but it is the archaic social gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: To tutor someone is to coach them, giving private instruction.
